utility.name: PHP 7.4 (sury, Debian 12 Bookworm)
utility.author: Thomas Shaw
utility.description:
Installs PHP 7.4 from the deb.sury.org third-party apt repository alongside Debian 12's own PHP 8.2, then makes 7.4 the default PHP for both the CLI (`update-alternatives --set php`) and, once Apache is present, the apache2 PHP handler module. This is additional software, not a downgrade of any system package: php8.2 is left installed.
This exists for vulnerability modules whose exploit needs PHP 7 semantics that PHP 8 changed or removed (e.g. a `?>` close tag is tolerated inside eval() under PHP 7 but is a parse error under PHP 8). Because it changes the host-wide default PHP, it conflicts with every other module known at the time of writing to install or depend on a particular PHP version, so SecGen's resolver will not compose it onto the same system as one of them. This is a point-in-time, best-effort list, not a guarantee: see manifests/install.pp for exactly what it does and does not protect against, and for why it does not touch Apache itself (left to the consuming module).
